1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Nc3 e5 4.Bc4 Be7 5.d.strategy: Supports e4 with a pawn and opens the c1 bishop. White gives up the idea of opening the centre and plays a slow, safe build-up, keeping the pressure on f7 and the control of d5 in the background.

Props up the e5 pawn with a pawn and opens the c8 bishop, giving Black a compact structure with no obvious target. Black accepts a slightly passive game in which White's pieces have more room and White holds the d5 square.

Develops with a direct hit on e4, keeping the active ...d5 strike in mind instead of the slower pawn move. But the knight blocks the bishop's view of g5, so White can bring a knight there to double the pressure on f7, and Black has to be ready for it.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Nc3 e5 4.Bc4 Be7 5.d.name: Sicilian Defence: Closed, Anti-Sveshnikov Variation, with Nf6
